clue.text: Be impertinent to artist and priest in Beaconsfield

parts.note: to dis someone is slang for treating them with disrespect
RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Someone is rude to a painter and a clergyman in a Buckinghamshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Beaconsfield is a town in Buckinghamshire, England, but here it stands for the statesman who was made Earl of Beaconsfield.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian Prime Minister took the title Earl of Beaconsfield in 1876, so the title names the man.

clue.text: Bearded author with script showing old instruments

parts.note: George Bernard Shaw, the playwright famous for his beard
MS is short for manuscript, a handwritten script

explanation.surface: A bearded writer's manuscript shows ancient musical instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: Shawms are medieval woodwind instruments with double reeds, forerunners of the oboe.

clue.text: Henry joins in expression of disapproval, missing nothing

indicators.note: the unit letter enters the middle of the jeer, so the jeer is cut open to take it

parts.note: a catcall is a whistle or shout of disapproval from an audience
H is the symbol for the henry, the SI unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A man called Henry joins the jeering crowd, not missing a thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry looks like a person's name but is the physics unit, abbreviated H.
explanation.definitionFit: Something all-embracing that leaves nothing out is a catch-all, as in a catch-all clause.

clue.text: Core feature of a tragedian's word to criticise 24-25's 11s

parts.note: the core of something is its middle

indicators.note: only the central feature of the word tragedian is kept, its outer letters falling away

explanation.surface: The central trait of a tragic actor is a term used to attack the broadcaster's men.
explanation.walkthrough: The core of TRagedIAN is AGED, so the clue says the core of 'tragedian' is middle AGED. Janet Street-Porter (24-25) attacked British TV bosses as male, middle-aged, middle-class and mediocre.
explanation.definitionFit: Street-Porter's famous complaint listed middle-aged among the traits of the men running television, so the term was her criticism.

clue.text: A particular Christian's superior, last to admit evil

parts.note: Fletcher Christian mutinied against his captain, William Bligh, on the Bounty

indicators.note: the final letter of the word admit is the one taken

explanation.surface: A Christian believer's boss is the last to own up to wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Christian' suggests a believer, but it is Fletcher Christian, leader of the mutiny on HMS Bounty, whose commanding officer was Captain Bligh.
explanation.definitionFit: A blight is a malign influence that spoils things, close to an evil in the general sense.

clue.text: Conductor offering drinks to travellers, maybe!

definitions.meaning: a ... is a metal strip conducting electricity in a switchboard
read as two words, a bar on a bus where passengers could buy a drink

explanation.definitionFit: Electricians call a thick metal conducting strip a busbar; split, it jokingly becomes a drinks counter on a coach.

clue.text: Decay of one beset by worries

indicators.note: the single letter is surrounded by the worries, so they go around it

parts.note: cares are worries
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone harassed by troubles is gradually going to pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Caries is the medical name for decay of teeth or bone.

clue.text: Say that's beyond the bounds of fool!

definitions.text: Say that's beyond the bounds of fool!

indicators.note: the first word sits outside the fool, enclosing it on both sides

parts.note: taken as written
a nit or nitwit is a fool

explanation.surface: An exclamation that sound judgement lies out of a fool's reach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beyond the bounds of' means the first word sits round the fool, and the whole clue doubles as definition: soundness of mind is just what lies out of a fool's reach.
explanation.definitionFit: Soundness of mind is the quality a fool lacks, so it lies outside his range.

clue.text: Tarnished record embarrassed one ex-Tory PM

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
red in the face from embarrassment
I is the Roman numeral for one
Ted Heath, Conservative Prime Minister 1970-74

explanation.surface: A former Conservative leader was shamed by a damaging record.
explanation.walkthrough: Ted Heath was the British Conservative Prime Minister of the early 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: A reputation that has been tarnished has been discredited, damaged in standing.

clue.text: One's held in custody — in poorer health, about to catch cold

indicators.note: the turned word catches the letter for cold, taking it inside
about signals that the word for poorer health is read backwards

parts.note: worse means feeling more ill
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A prisoner, sicker than before, is about to come down with a cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns WORSE into ESROW, and 'to catch' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An escrow is a deed or money held by a third party until a condition is met, a kind of custody.

clue.text: Official order to blockade islands when there's a disturbance

indicators.note: the order surrounds the islands as a blockade would

parts.note: an indent is an official requisition for supplies
CI stands for the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: A government decree imposes a naval blockade on islands during unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands (CI) are British islands off the coast of France.
explanation.definitionFit: An incident can mean a violent disturbance or clash, as in border incidents.

clue.text: Part of 24-25's description of management post for the audience

indicators.note: what an audience hears is the word spoken, so it is how the word sounds

parts.note: mail is post, letters delivered

explanation.surface: A journalist's account of a management job is broadcast to listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: Janet Street-Porter (24-25) described TV management as male, middle-aged, middle-class and mediocre.
explanation.definitionFit: Being men was the first trait in her list describing the bosses running television.

clue.text: Act, oarsmen being in trouble in US river

indicators.note: letters in trouble are thrown into disorder, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rowers get into difficulty on an American river and must act.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sacramento is the main river of California, flowing into San Francisco Bay.

clue.text: Note (as the answer here) female's assessment of certain 11s (24-25's)

parts.note: middle C is the note at the centre of the keyboard, and the answer does begin with that word
a lass is a girl or woman

explanation.surface: A woman's verdict on certain men, with a musical note attached.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'female' is 'is', linking the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Street-Porter's list called television's bosses middle-class as well as male, so the term was her judgement of them.

clue.text: Act to stifle silly chat, being aloof

indicators.note: the act wraps round the chatter and smothers it

parts.note: a deed is an act

indicators.note: silly chat is chat in a muddled order

explanation.surface: Doing something to quell foolish gossip, while remaining distant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' rearranges the chat into TACH, which 'to stifle' smothers inside the act. 'Act' looks like a verb but is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone detached keeps emotionally apart, which is what aloof means.

clue.text: It's natural to keep in step and fail to be vibrant

indicators.note: the step holds the natural inside it

parts.note: a stage is a step in a process

explanation.surface: It is only natural to march in time and lose all your liveliness.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagnate is to stop developing and become dull and inactive.

clue.text: Conservative religious school into very big tricks

indicators.note: the school goes inside the size label

parts.note: OS is the clothing label for outsize
Zen is a school of Buddhism

explanation.surface: A Tory religious school takes on enormous deceptions.
explanation.definitionFit: To cozen is an old verb meaning to cheat or deceive.

clue.text: Recovered from booze, not wanting any brought in

indicators.note: the abstainer's mark is placed inside the drink

parts.note: beer is booze
TT means teetotal, refusing all alcohol

explanation.surface: Someone recovers from a drinking session by refusing any more.
explanation.definitionFit: Being better is having got over an illness, the sense of recovered.

clue.text: Thinking no more of winning? In favour of coming first!

indicators.note: the phrase for supporting is placed before the word for winning

parts.note: for means in favour of
getting, as in winning or gaining

explanation.surface: Is victory no longer a concern? Supporters put it first!
explanation.definitionFit: Forgetting something means no longer having it in mind, ceasing to think of it.

clue.text: Charm of AR's successor repeatedly evident

indicators.note: the cipher is given twice in a row

parts.note: Queen Anne (Anna Regina, AR) was followed by George I, Georgius Rex the first, GR I

explanation.surface: A lucky charm from the queen's successor keeps cropping up.
explanation.walkthrough: AR is Queen Anne's royal cipher, Anna Regina; her successor was George I, written GR I.
explanation.definitionFit: A grigri is an African amulet or talisman worn as a lucky charm.

clue.text: Meat good for offering to pagan god

parts.note: Ammon is the ancient Egyptian god, also called Amun

explanation.surface: Fine meat as a sacrifice to a heathen deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Gammon is cured or smoked ham from the hind leg of a pig.

clue.text: See 4
First person (terrible) to hold company back (like 11s slammed by 24-25)

parts.note: me is the first person pronoun

indicators.note: the word for terrible holds the turned company

parts.note: dire means terrible

indicators.note: back signals that the company's abbreviation is read in reverse

explanation.surface: I, dreadful as I am, keep a firm going in reverse, like the men a critic attacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the company into OC; 'to hold' puts it inside the word for terrible. Street-Porter (24-25) called TV's male bosses mediocre among other things.
explanation.definitionFit: Mediocre, merely ordinary, was the last of Street-Porter's charges against television's male bosses.

clue.text: Baby at home keeping silent? On the contrary

indicators.note: one piece keeps the other inside it
the roles are swapped, so it is the silent word that holds the home word, not the other way

parts.note: mute means silent
in means at home

explanation.surface: Is a quiet infant at home? No, the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baby' is an adjective meaning tiny, as in baby carrots.
explanation.definitionFit: Baby as an adjective means very small, and minute means tiny.

clue.text: The way beer satisfies a journalist

parts.note: a street is a way or road
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: Ale on the road keeps a newspaper writer happy.
explanation.walkthrough: Janet Street-Porter is a British journalist and broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Janet Street-Porter is a British journalist and former television executive, so she is an example of one.

clue.text: See 24
